mnemonic: flip(轻弹)+pant→轻飘飘的，「轻率的」。
example: His flippant answer to the serious question offended the panel.
exampleCn: 他对这个严肃问题的轻率回答冒犯了评审团。

mnemonic: 联想 foam(泡沫)+ment→搅起泡沫，「煽动」。
example: The speech fomented unrest among the workers demanding better wages.
exampleCn: 这场演讲在要求涨薪的工人中煽动了动荡。

mnemonic: for+bear(忍受)+ance→「忍耐」。
example: The teacher showed remarkable forbearance with the disruptive student.
exampleCn: 老师对那个捣乱的学生表现出极大的忍耐。

mnemonic: fortu(运气，同 fortune)+itous→靠运气的，偶然的。
example: Their meeting at the conference was entirely fortuitous, not arranged in advance.
exampleCn: 他们在会议上的相遇纯属偶然，并非事先安排。

mnemonic: fract(碎，同 fracture)+ious→动不动就碎、发火，易怒的。
example: The fractious crowd grew restless after hours of waiting in the rain.
exampleCn: 在雨中等了几个小时后，易怒的人群变得焦躁不安。

mnemonic: 联想 freight(货物)满载→充满忧虑。
example: The negotiation was fraught with tension and mutual suspicion.
exampleCn: 这场谈判充满紧张和相互猜疑。

mnemonic: friv(轻，同 frivolity 轻浮)+olous→轻浮无聊的。
example: The committee dismissed the proposal as frivolous and not worth funding.
exampleCn: 委员会认为该提案无聊，不值得资助。

mnemonic: fruit(果实)+ion→结出果实，实现。
example: After years of research, the project finally came to fruition.
exampleCn: 经过多年研究，这个项目终于结出成果。

mnemonic: fur(皮毛，转指躲藏)+tive→偷偷摸摸像躲藏，鬼祟的。
example: He cast a furtive glance at the answer sheet during the exam.
exampleCn: 考试时他偷偷瞥了一眼答题纸。

mnemonic: garr(喋喋，同 garrulity)+ulous→唠叨的。
example: The garrulous guide talked throughout the entire bus tour without pausing.
exampleCn: 那位唠叨的导游在整个巴士行程中不停地说。

mnemonic: 法语借词，谐音「够失」→够失礼，不得体。
example: His gauche attempt at small talk made the dinner awkward for everyone.
exampleCn: 他笨拙的搭讪尝试让晚餐对每个人都很尴尬。

mnemonic: german(德国的)联想→同根同源才相关，切题的。
example: Please keep your comments germane to the topic under discussion.
exampleCn: 请让你的评论与正在讨论的话题相关。

mnemonic: 联想 glide(滑行)→说话油滑流畅但空洞。
example: His glib promises sounded convincing but lacked any concrete plan.
exampleCn: 他油滑的承诺听起来可信，却缺乏任何具体计划。

mnemonic: grand(宏大)+iose→宏大浮夸的。
example: The grandiose plan to build a city in the desert was never funded.
exampleCn: 那个在沙漠中建城的浮夸计划从未获得资助。

mnemonic: gratu(感谢，同 gratuity 小费)+itous→本是免费，引申为无端无故。
example: The film was criticized for its gratuitous violence against innocent characters.
exampleCn: 这部电影因对无辜角色无端的暴力而受批评。

mnemonic: greg(群，同 congregate 聚集)+arious→群居的；反 solitary。
example: Wolves are gregarious animals that hunt and live in coordinated packs.
exampleCn: 狼是群居动物，成群协调地捕猎和生活。

mnemonic: 联想 beguile(欺骗)→狡猾诡计。
example: He achieved his goals through patience rather than guile and deception.
exampleCn: 他靠耐心而非狡猾和欺骗达成目标。

mnemonic: hackney(旧式出租马车)+ed→像旧车一样老套。
example: The writer avoided hackneyed phrases and sought fresh images for her prose.
exampleCn: 这位作家避免陈腐的套话，为散文寻找新鲜意象。

mnemonic: 希腊神话 halcyon(翠鸟)→传说能使海面平静，平静的。
example: The town enjoyed a halcyon period of peace and prosperity after the war.
exampleCn: 战后这个小镇享受了一段平静繁荣的时期。

mnemonic: hap(机会，同 happen)+hazard(冒险)→随机会冒险，随意杂乱。
example: The files were stored in a haphazard manner, making retrieval difficult.
exampleCn: 这些文件以杂乱的方式存放，难以取用。

mnemonic: har+bin(篮)+ger→带来消息的人，先兆。
example: The early snowfall was a harbinger of a particularly harsh winter.
exampleCn: 早来的降雪是特别严冬的预兆。

mnemonic: haught(高，同 high)+y→自视甚高，傲慢的。
example: Her haughty manner made her unpopular among her classmates.
exampleCn: 她傲慢的态度使她在同学中不受欢迎。

mnemonic: hedon(快乐，同 hedonism)+istic→追求快乐的，享乐主义。
example: The critic described the novel's hero as selfish and hedonistic.
exampleCn: 评论家把这部小说的主人公描述为自私而享乐主义的。

mnemonic: heg(领导)+emony→领导权，霸权。
example: The empire maintained its hegemony over the region for nearly a century.
exampleCn: 这个帝国在该地区的霸权维持了近一个世纪。

mnemonic: her(传令)+ald→传令官，引申为预示。
example: The invention of the printing press heralded a new era of learning.
exampleCn: 印刷术的发明预示着一个知识新时代的到来。

mnemonic: hetero(不同)+gene(种)+ous→不同种类，异质的；反 homogeneous。
example: The sample was heterogeneous, containing rocks of widely varying compositions.
exampleCn: 这个样本是异质的，含有成分差异很大的岩石。

mnemonic: hi(张口)+atus→张开裂缝，中断。
example: There was a brief hiatus in the lecture when the projector failed.
exampleCn: 投影仪故障时讲座有一小段中断。

mnemonic: homo(人)+ge→像人一样低头致敬。
example: The young painter paid homage to the masters of the Renaissance.
exampleCn: 这位年轻画家向文艺复兴大师们致敬。

mnemonic: hyper(过度，同 hyperactive)+bole(抛)→话抛过头，夸张。
example: The advertisement used hyperbole, claiming the product would change your life overnight.
exampleCn: 这则广告用了夸张手法，声称产品会一夜改变你的生活。

cn: 打破传统者；偶像破坏者
mnemonic: icon(偶像)+clast(破坏，同 plastic)→破坏偶像者。
example: As an iconoclast, the artist rejected the conventions of his time.
exampleCn: 作为打破传统者，这位艺术家摒弃了他那个时代的常规。

mnemonic: idio(个人，同 idiom)+syn(共同)+crasy(混合)→个人独有的特质。
example: Every researcher has idiosyncrasies that shape how they design experiments.
exampleCn: 每位研究者都有影响其实验设计方式的个人特质。

mnemonic: ign(不，同 ignore)+nomin(名声，同 nominal)+ious→名声尽失，可耻的。
example: The team suffered an ignominious defeat in the final match.
exampleCn: 这支队伍在决赛中遭受了可耻的失败。

mnemonic: il(不)+licit(合法，同 license)→非法的。
example: The merchant was fined for selling illicit goods without a permit.
exampleCn: 这名商人因无照出售非法商品被罚款。

mnemonic: illus(欺骗，同 illusion)+ory→虚幻的。
example: The promised benefits proved illusory once the contract was examined closely.
exampleCn: 仔细审查合同后，承诺的好处被证明是虚幻的。

mnemonic: im(不)+macul(斑点)+ate→无斑点，洁净无瑕。
example: The surgical room was kept immaculate to prevent any risk of infection.
exampleCn: 手术室保持绝对洁净，以防止任何感染风险。

mnemonic: im(不)+mut(改变，同 mutate)+able→不可改变的。
example: The laws of physics are considered immutable under ordinary conditions.
exampleCn: 在通常条件下，物理定律被认为是不变的。

mnemonic: im(不)+pass(通过)+e→无法通过，僵局。
example: The talks reached an impasse when neither side would compromise.
exampleCn: 由于双方都不肯妥协，会谈陷入僵局。

mnemonic: im(不)+pass(感情，同 passion)+ive→不动感情，无表情的。
example: He remained impassive throughout the trial, revealing no emotion at all.
exampleCn: 整个审判过程中他面无表情，毫无情绪流露。

mnemonic: im(不)+pecc(罪，同 peccant)+able→无过失，无可挑剔。
example: Her command of the language was impeccable, impressing the entire audience.
exampleCn: 她对语言的掌握无可挑剔，打动了全场听众。

mnemonic: im(不)+pertin(属于，同 pertinent)+ent→不相干还插嘴，无礼的。
example: His impertinent question about her age embarrassed the whole class.
exampleCn: 他关于她年龄的无礼问题让全班都很尴尬。

mnemonic: im(不)+perv(穿过，同 permeate)+ious→穿不过，不透的。
example: The coating makes the fabric impervious to water and stains.
exampleCn: 这种涂层使织物不透水和污渍。

cn: 无法安抚的；深仇难解的
mnemonic: im(不)+plac(安抚，同 placate)+able→无法安抚的。
example: The two families maintained an implacable hostility for generations.
exampleCn: 两家人数代保持着无法化解的敌意。

mnemonic: im+plic(折叠，同 complicate)+ate→把人折进案子，牵连。
example: The evidence implicated several officials in the corruption scandal.
exampleCn: 证据把几名官员牵连进这起腐败丑闻。

mnemonic: im+pug(打，同 pugilist 拳手)+n→抨击质疑。
example: No one dared to impugn the authority of the renowned scholar.
exampleCn: 没人敢质疑这位著名学者的权威。

mnemonic: in(不)+ane(呼吸，同 animate)→没气的，空洞愚蠢。
example: The sitcom relied on inane jokes that failed to make anyone laugh.
exampleCn: 这部情景喜剧依赖空洞的笑料，没逗笑任何人。

mnemonic: in+cand(白，同 candidate 白袍)+escent→烧到发白，炽热的。
example: The incandescent bulb glowed warmly in the dark laboratory.
exampleCn: 白炽灯泡在黑暗的实验室里发出温暖的光。

mnemonic: in+cip(开始，同 inception)+ient→初期的。
example: Engineers detected an incipient fault in the machine before it failed.
exampleCn: 工程师在机器故障前检测到初期的问题。

mnemonic: in(不)+congru(一致，同 congruous)+ous→不协调的。
example: The modern sculpture looked incongruous among the ancient ruins.
exampleCn: 这座现代雕塑在古代遗迹中显得不协调。

cn: 屡教不改的；不可救药的
mnemonic: in(不)+corrig(纠正，同 correct)+ible→无法纠正的。
example: The incorrigible prankster was repeatedly warned but never changed his ways.
exampleCn: 这个屡教不改的恶作剧者一再被警告却从不改。

cn: 不知疲倦的；坚持不懈的
mnemonic: in(不)+de+fatig(疲劳，同 fatigue)+able→不知疲倦。
example: Her indefatigable efforts finally secured the funding for the library.
exampleCn: 她坚持不懈的努力终于为图书馆争取到了经费。
